author: Gabriella Morando
title: Marion and Howard County first responders recovering after Thursday attacks - NewsBreak
text:
By Gabriella Morando ,
3 hours ago
MARION COUNTY, Ind. — First responders in both Marion and Howard Counties are getting checked out after being attacked Thursday. Police have not made any indication that the two incidents, in Indianapolis and Kokomo, are connected.
Around 7 a.m., IMPD responded to a report of a person trying to break into cars near Lugar Tower Apartments downtown. Officers made contact with what they called a "suspicious person.” That person then assaulted one of the officers and took off in a car.
The officer was taken to the hospital in stable condition. FOX59/CBS4 reached out to officials Thursday afternoon asking if the officer had been released, but did not receive a response.
Authorities said they are working to track down the suspect. FOP Lodge 86 Vice President Bobby Ferguson said that while information is still limited, the impact is undeniable.
“Not only does it take a toll on the officer, but their family, fellow co-workers and the community,” Ferguson said. “When you assault an officer, you're assaulting public safety in general.”
A few hours later, members of the Kokomo Fire Department were “cussed out and spit on” during an annual fundraiser.
The department said, while no one was injured, at least one crew member was checked out after possibly being contaminated by bodily fluid. Officials were not available for an interview about the incident and the suspect, but wrote on social media that the suspect “is obviously having some type of psychological issue.”
“If someone does happen to go through a mental health crisis or is struggling that day, reach out, ask for help,” Ferguson said. “Any one of us would be more than happy to help an individual going through a mental health crisis.”
Kokomo Police have identified, but not yet located the suspect. A spokesperson said a warrant request is being submitted.
Again, police have not indicated that the two incidents, in Marion and Howard Counties, are connected. The investigations into both are ongoing.
